source.title: Learning with noisy labels via clean aware sharpness aware minimization
source.authors: Bin Huang; Ying Xie; Chao-Yang Xu

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Table 2 is flattened and its values cannot be reliably assigned to methods and conditions.
record.tranche_reason: The paper builds CA-SAM around sharpness-aware minimization for noisy-label learning. Its benchmark comparisons report the performance of that new method; they do not test the claim versions’ specified conditions or measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses overfitting to noisy labels and sharpness, and reports qualitative loss-landscape observations plus noisy-label benchmark accuracy. The benchmark tables compare CA-SAM with other methods; Table 1 results are explicitly taken from original papers. No arbitrary-label memorization test, width sweep, convolution-versus-fully-connected comparison, optimizer comparison under the stated tuning conditions, batch-size comparison, dropout test, magnitude-aware sharpness measure, or memorized-example removal test is reported.
record.test_reason: The study uses the sharpness–generalization connection to develop CA-SAM and evaluates noisy-label classification performance. Its qualitative loss landscapes do not measure V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance or its association with generalization gaps among similarly fitted models. No other claim version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that using historically identified likely clean samples to determine weight perturbations improves noisy-label learning. They report competitive benchmark accuracy, acknowledge weaker robustness than hybrid methods at high noise, and propose label correction as future work.
record.recipe_differences: CA-SAM uses historical outputs to divide noisy-label training samples and uses likely clean samples to determine the SAM perturbation direction; it is evaluated on synthetic and real-world noisy-label benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise level and the CA-SAM neighborhood parameter ρ affect reported performance; at 80% noise, ρ values 0.2 and 0.5 cause model collapse. The authors say performance is weaker than hybrid methods at the highest tested noise levels.

fits_no_version.finding: At epoch 100 on CIFAR-10 with 60% symmetric noise, SGD has flat landscapes but high loss; SAM has approximately 0.1 loss but relatively sharp landscapes; CA-SAM has lower clean-data loss than SGD and a flatter clean-data landscape than SAM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Clean-sample-directed SAM perturbations can improve the combination of training loss and qualitative landscape flatness during noisy-label learning.

fits_no_version.finding: CA-SAM's noisy-label benchmark performance depends on noise level and perturbation radius; at 80% noise, radii 0.2 and 0.5 cause collapse. The authors report weaker high-noise robustness than hybrid methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CA-SAM improves noisy-label classification in some settings, with robustness depending on noise severity and perturbation configuration.

record.problems: The landscape evidence is qualitative and does not quantify a training–test gap. Table 2 is flattened, so its method-to-value assignments cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied text. Several benchmark comparisons are identified as sourced from prior work.
record.rows_left_out: No benchmark accuracy rows were extracted: the reported comparisons evaluate the proposed noisy-label method, while the source text does not provide a clean assignment for Table 2 and the other benchmark tables do not test a claim version’s specified intervention or measurement. Table 1 is explicitly sourced from original papers.

untested.parts: Matched natural-label and fixed-random-label training, near-perfect random-label fit, and corresponding held-out accuracies.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, measured generalization gaps among similarly fitted models, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing examples selected by label memorization influence versus removing equally many random examples, followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Partial label corruption is not V1's fixed-random-label memorization experiment. The radius sweep tunes CA-SAM rather than measuring V7's perturbation tolerance. Benchmark results and ablations omitted from the rows are already declared in rows_left_out and do not supply missing tests of a claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out accuracy on natural labels.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the stated tuning conditions.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and its interaction with data augmentation and weight decay.
The study does not measure magnitude-scaled weight perturbation tolerance or rank generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
